Start working on Linear ticket eng-2114 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2114` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2114`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `turbo dev --F=roam`
- **Obsidian**: `export SUPABASE_USE_DB=local && turbo dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn $(pwd)/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

Explored the code. Here's the plan.

## Context found

- [NodeSearchModal.tsx](.claude/worktrees/eng-2114-insert-active-result-as-a-link-at-cursor/apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx) already reserves the keystroke — `handleKeyDown` has `// Mod+Enter and Alt+Enter are left alone for the insert and dock actions.`
- [NodeSearchFooter.tsx](.claude/worktrees/eng-2114-insert-active-result-as-a-link-at-cursor/apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchFooter.tsx) is the ENG-2113 skeleton: a `FooterAction` + `KeyHints` pair, `canAct` gate.
- The Roam analog is [advancedSearchFooterUtils.ts](apps/roam/src/utils/advancedSearchFooterUtils.ts) (`snapshotInsertTarget` / `insertPageRefAtRange`) and the footer hides the action entirely when `insertTarget` is null — I'll mirror that shape.
- Modal is opened from [registerCommands.ts:146](.claude/worktrees/eng-2114-insert-active-result-as-a-link-at-cursor/apps/obsidian/src/utils/registerCommands.ts:146).

## Plan

**1. New util — `apps/obsidian/src/utils/editorInsertTarget.ts`**
- `type EditorInsertTarget = { view: MarkdownView; from: EditorPosition; to: EditorPosition }`
- `snapshotInsertTarget(app): EditorInsertTarget | null` — `app.workspace.getActiveViewOfType(MarkdownView)`, bail if none or if `view.getMode() !== "source"` (reading mode has no cursor), else capture `editor.getCursor("from")` and `getCursor("to")` so a selection gets replaced rather than orphaned (matches Roam).
- `insertLinkAtInsertTarget({ app, target, file })` — `app.fileManager.generateMarkdownLink(file, target.view.file.path)`, then `editor.replaceRange(link, from, to)`, `editor.setCursor` past the link, `app.workspace.setActiveLeaf(view.leaf, { focus: true })` + `editor.focus()`.

**2. Snapshot in the `NodeSearchModal` constructor, not `onOpen`**
The constructor runs at command-callback time — before `open()` mounts the modal and moves focus. Store it as a private field and pass it into `<NodeSearch insertTarget={...} />`.

**3. Wire the action in `NodeSearch`**
- `handleInsertLink()`: guard on `activeResult && insertTarget`, `onClose()` first (unmounts the root, same ordering discipline as `openActiveResult`), then insert; `new Notice(...)` on failure.
- In `handleKeyDown`, add a Mod+Enter branch **above** the existing `if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey) return;` early-out.

**4. Footer**
- Add `insertTarget`-derived props; render `<FooterAction keys={["Mod", "Enter"]} label="insert link at cursor" />` only when a target exists, disabled when `!canAct`. Placed first, matching Roam's order.

## Two things to flag

1. **`editor.hasFocus()` is not a usable gate.** Opening the search from the command palette means the palette modal already took focus, so a `hasFocus()` check would hide the action on the primary invocation path. I'm reading "no editor was focused at open time" as "no active Markdown view in source mode" instead. Tell me if you want it stricter.
2. **No test infra in `apps/obsidian`** — no vitest, no `test` script (roam, website, database, content-model have it; obsidian doesn't). So per-project convention there are no unit tests to write here. Verification will be manual against the running Obsidian over CDP: insert into a note mid-word, confirm the link lands at the pre-open cursor, toggle vault link settings (wikilink ↔ markdown, shortest path ↔ absolute) and re-check the format, confirm focus returns, and confirm the action is absent when invoked from reading mode / with no note open.

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with

Answering the md question directly:

**Text: yes. Images inside it: no, not on their own.**

- `gh pr create --body-file verification.md` (or `gh pr comment --body-file`) works fine — that's fully scriptable, and it's how I'd set the body.
- But **attaching a `.md` file to a comment doesn't render it** — GitHub shows an attached file as a download link, not as formatted content.
- And image paths inside the md only render if they're absolute URLs GitHub can fetch. Relative paths don't resolve in PR bodies or comments (only in files rendered from the repo tree). So `![x](01-insert.gif)` renders as a broken image.

The `github.com/user-attachments/assets/…` URLs your PR #1294 uses come from **drag-and-drop in the browser**; there's no public API or `gh` command for that endpoint.

So there are three real routes:

| Route | Scriptable | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| You drag the 6 gifs into a PR comment once, I rewrite the md with the URLs GitHub hands back, then `gh pr edit --body-file` | Half — one manual drop | Matches existing convention (#1294) |
| Push artifacts to a non-merged `assets/eng-2114` branch, reference `raw.githubusercontent.com/…` URLs | Fully | Binaries live in the repo's object store forever |
| `gh release upload` to a draft release | Fully | Abuses releases for review artifacts |

My recommendation is the first: drop the gifs into the PR, paste me the comment, and I'll splice the URLs into the body. One 10-second manual step, no repo pollution.

## What the capture pass does now

`CAPTURE=1 node verify-eng-2114.mjs` — off by default, so ordinary runs stay fast. Per scenario it records a gif via `Page.startScreencast`, using each frame's `metadata.timestamp` to build an ffmpeg concat list with **real per-frame durations**, so playback matches the pace the run actually happened rather than a guessed frame rate. Stills come from `Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip` derived from `getBoundingClientRect()`, so the footer shots are tight crops rather than full-window.

content.text:
Done — and the fix wasn't the encoder. Here's the reasoning, since it changes what "slow it down" should mean.

## Why they were unwatchable

The driver acts at machine speed: `executeCommandById` opens the modal in one frame, `replaceRange` inserts in one frame. The screencast only emits frames when pixels change, so there were **no intermediate frames to watch** — nothing to slow down. Stretching playback would just hold each already-confusing frame longer.

So the pacing has to be created in the *run*, not the encode.

## Alternatives, and what I picked

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Time-stretch the existing gif | Rejected — sluggish, still unexplained |
| **Pause the driver at semantic beats + burn in captions** | **Implemented** — the state holds 2.6s with a numbered label explaining it |
| **Type at human speed (90ms/char)** | **Implemented** — you can read the query forming |
| **mp4 instead of gif** | **Implemented as primary** — GitHub renders it with scrub/pause/replay, so the reviewer controls the pace. Also 40× smaller |
| Collapse sidebars | Implemented — tighter frame, and a privacy fix (see below) |
| Numbered still-strip instead of motion | Still available if you'd rather have zero-timing artifacts; the per-scenario stills are already captured |

Scenarios now declare their own narration: `await beat("Node search opens — the editor has lost focus, but the cursor was already snapshotted.")`. Each beat grabs a still, appends it as an explicitly-timed frame, and gets its caption burned over exactly that stretch via `drawtext` with an `enable='between(t,…)'` range. Clips run **12–29s** with 2–5 captions each. Gif is now opt-in (`GIF=1`).

## Three bugs found while doing it

1. **A 90-second clip.** Frame durations came from timestamp deltas, so an idle stretch — waiting on Obsidian's debounced save — inflated one frame to 60s+. Clamped to 900ms.
2. **Captions collapsing to nothing.** I first derived spans from screencast frame indices; several beats landed on the same index, so their spans were zero-width. Beats now own a dedicated frame.
3. **The `hasFocus` assertion was measuring macOS, not the plugin.** It failed twice in one run, and I nearly filed it as a defect. A probe showed `document.hasFocus()` is `false` whenever the terminal is frontmost — and CodeMirror's `hasFocus()` ANDs with that, so running `pnpm build` before a run flipped it. The assertion now checks `document.activeElement` is inside `.cm-editor`, which is what "focus returned to the editor" actually means, and reports `documentHasFocus` alongside for context. **This was a bad assertion, not a flake** — my earlier "it was a flake" call was half right: environmental, but reproducible once you know the trigger.

Also: `⌘↵` was rendering as tofu boxes — Arial has neither glyph. Switched to Arial Unicode.

## Two things you should look at

1. **Your `.env` is done** — both the main repo and this worktree now mirror to `testVault` only, originals kept as `.env.bak-eng2114`. `testVault2` still holds the last build mirrored there.
2. **The old gifs had your private Claude chat pane in frame** — right sidebar, visible mid-conversation text. The new runs collapse both sidebars, but if you'd already planned to post the earlier gifs, don't.

# Checkpoint — record session context

Persist the **reasoning layer** of this work session (goal, decisions, dead ends,
constraints, next step) to the Obsidian vault, keyed to the current worktree.
Files are plain markdown written directly — no MCP, no Obsidian required running.

## Steps

### 1. Resolve where to write
Run the helper from the current worktree:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

It prints `TICKET`, `BRANCH`, `WORKTREE`, `SESSION_DIR`, `CONTEXT_FILE`,
`LOG_FILE`, `STAMP`, `CONTEXT_EXISTS` and creates the folders. **Only write to the
`CONTEXT_FILE` and `LOG_FILE` paths it gives you** — never elsewhere in the vault.
If it errors (not a git repo / detached HEAD), tell the user and stop.

### 2. Read existing context if present
If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, read `CONTEXT_FILE` first so you UPDATE it rather than
overwrite history. Digest sections get rewritten; accreting sections get appended.

### 3. Gather the reasoning layer
Reconstruct from this session's conversation + git. If a ticket id is present and
Linear is available, you may fetch the title/URL with `mcp__linear-server__get_issue`.
Apply the **extraction rubric** below to decide what is worth recording.

### 4. Write `_context.md`
Use the template at `~/.claude/skills/checkpoint/template.md` as the structure.
- If new file: fill the template. Set `created`/`updated` to today, `sessions: 1`.
- If updating: rewrite digest sections (TL;DR, Current state, Next step, Open
  questions, key_files, status), **append** to accreting sections (Key decisions,
  Dead ends, Constraints, Gotchas) with a dated bullet, bump `updated` to today
  and increment `sessions`.

### 5. Append a log snapshot
Write a short dated entry to `LOG_FILE` (a fresh file — no append needed):
a 3–6 line summary of what THIS session accomplished + what changed since last time.
This is the immutable audit trail; `_context.md` is the living digest.

### 6. Confirm
Tell the user what you wrote (context file + log file paths) and the one-line Next step.

## Extraction rubric — what to record (keep it concise)

**The test:** record a line only if it would otherwise have to be *re-derived* or
would prevent *repeating a mistake*. Ask: *"What do I know now that I didn't at
session start, that isn't already in Linear, git, or the code?"*

**DO record (the reasoning layer — it evaporates when the session ends):**
- Scope agreement: how the ticket was interpreted, what's in/out of scope.
- Decisions: what + why + what was rejected + what would make us revisit it.
- Dead ends: what was tried that failed, and why.
- Constraints/preferences the user stated ("ship by Fri", "don't touch billing").
- Gotchas: environmental facts learned the hard way.
- Next step + open questions + current status.

**Do NOT record (noise / lives elsewhere):**
- Activity logs ("edited foo.ts, ran tests") — record outcomes, not keystrokes.
- Anything copy-pasteable from the diff, git history, or the Linear ticket body.
- Resolved questions — delete them or fold the answer into a decision.
- Restating how the code works — that's what the code is for.

**Mark uncertainty** explicitly (`*assumed*`, `*unchecked*`). Prefer 8 sharp lines
over 40 vague ones — this must stay skimmable for the user, not just parseable by an agent.

# Verify Obsidian plugin changes over CDP

`apps/obsidian` has no test runner (roam, website, database and content-model do).
The way to prove a change works is to drive the real app: Obsidian is Electron, so
it speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol. About 150 lines covers `evaluate`, input
injection, screenshots and screencast — Playwright is not required.

Two outputs come from one run: **assertions** for you, and **captioned mp4s** for
the PR.

## Prerequisites

1. **Relaunch Obsidian with the debug port.** Run the steps separately — the
   auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound command.
   ```bash
   osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to quit'
   ```
   ```bash
   open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222
   ```
   Ask the user before doing this: it closes their running app.
2. **`ffmpeg`** on PATH, only for the capture pass (`brew install ffmpeg`).
3. **Your build in the vault.** `apps/obsidian/.env` mirrors the dev build into
   the vault plugin dir. Confirm it is *your* build — see the first gotcha.

## Flow

```bash
# 1. preflight: port up, right vault, YOUR bundle, plugin enabled
node scripts/preflight.mjs "a string unique to your change"

# 2. assertions only — fast, run this repeatedly while iterating
node your-verification.mjs

# 3. once, when the branch is ready for a PR: assertions + captioned mp4s
CAPTURE=1 ARTIFACT_DIR=./artifacts node your-verification.mjs
```

Write the verification as scenarios and hand them to `runVerification`, which owns
everything order-dependent (plugin reload, stray-modal cleanup, sidebar collapse,
teardown, exit code):

```js
import { runVerification } from "./scripts/harness.mjs";

await runVerification({
  modalSelector: ".dg-node-search-modal",
  setup: async ({ client }) => ({ /* snapshot anything you will mutate */ }),
  teardown: async ({ client, state }) => { /* put it back */ },
  scenarios: [
    {
      name: "01-does-the-thing",
      body: async ({ client, check, beat, state }) => {
        await beat("Starting state a reviewer can recognise.");
        await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById("…");`);
        await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".my-modal")`, { label: "modal" });
        check("the thing happened", await client.evaluate(`…`), "detail on failure");
        await beat("What just changed, and why it proves the requirement.");
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

`client` gives you `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `screenshot`,
`rectOf`, `reloadPlugin`, `pressEscape`. `saveStill({ client, name, clipSelector })`
writes a clipped png. See `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` — the real
verification that shipped ENG-2114, 15 assertions across 3 scenarios.

## Making the recording watchable

The driver acts at machine speed: the modal opens in one frame, the edit lands in
the next. A raw recording has **nothing to watch between states**, and slowing
playback just holds confusing frames longer. Pacing has to be created in the run,
not the encode — that is what `beat("…")` is for. It grabs a still, holds it 2.6s,
and burns the text in over exactly that stretch as a numbered caption. Typing also
slows to 90ms/char under `CAPTURE=1`.

Aim for one beat per state a reviewer needs to recognise: the starting state, the
action, the outcome. Write them as claims about behaviour, not narration of
keystrokes.

## Getting the artifacts onto a PR

mp4 is the default output because GitHub gives it a scrub/pause player — the
reviewer controls the pace — and it runs ~40× smaller than the same clip as a gif
(1.1MB vs 31MB for six clips). Set `GIF=1` if you specifically need a gif.

**There is no API for PR image/video attachments.** The
`github.com/user-attachments/assets/…` URLs come from drag-and-drop in the browser
only. `gh pr create --body-file` handles the *text*; relative image paths do not
resolve in PR bodies. So: write the body with drop markers, drag the mp4s in, and
paste the URLs back. Limits are 10MB per image, 100MB per video.

## Gotchas

Each of these cost real debugging time. The first three produced confident, wrong
diagnoses.

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| "My feature is missing from the build" | **Every worktree's dev watcher mirrors into the same vault plugin dir.** Another branch's watcher silently overwrote your bundle. This is what `preflight.mjs` checks. Find competing watchers with `pgrep -fl "scripts/dev.ts"`; rebuild with `(cd apps/obsidian && pnpm build)`. |
| App appears to double-handle one keypress | Your key helper spread `{ type, ...opts }`, so a caller's `type: "keyDown"` overrode the loop and sent two keydowns. `type` must come **after** the spread. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` is false but focus looks right | CodeMirror ANDs with `document.hasFocus()`, so it reports false whenever Obsidian is not the frontmost macOS app — running a build in the terminal flips it. Assert `document.activeElement.closest(".cm-editor")` instead. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks correct | Obsidian saves on a debounce. Poll the file until it changes; never read straight after the action. |
| A 20-second run encodes to 90 seconds | Frame durations come from timestamp deltas and frames only arrive on change, so an idle wait inflates one frame. Clamp per-frame duration. |
| Captions vanish | Spans derived from screencast frame indices collapse when several beats land on one index. Each beat needs its own explicitly-timed frame. |
| Assertions read a mix of two modals | A crashed earlier run left one mounted. `runVerification` clears strays first; a synthetic `body.click()` will not dismiss a modal, an Escape key event will. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | You detached every markdown leaf first. Use `getLeaf("tab")`, which reuses an empty active leaf. |
| `⌘` and `↵` render as tofu boxes | Arial has neither glyph. Use `Arial Unicode.ttf`. |
| Editing only files under `src/styles/` never rebuilds | The concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd`, outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file. |
| Top-level `await` throws inside `evaluate` | Bodies are wrapped in a plain function. Return a promise chain instead. |
| Wrong window driven | Several page targets exist — one per open vault, plus popouts and settings. Select by `app.vault.getName()`, never by title. |

Two more, from experience rather than symptoms:

- **Reset state at the start of a scenario**, or assertions inherit leftover tabs
  and splits from the last run and a correct implementation reads as a failure.
- **The developer is using the app while you drive it.** A human opening a tab
  mid-run produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation.

## Privacy

Recordings capture the whole window, including whatever is docked in the sidebars —
other notes, chat panes. The capture pass collapses both sidebars for this reason
and restores them afterwards. Look at the frames before posting artifacts anywhere
public, and never publish a recording made before that collapse existed.

Verification runs also mutate the vault: scratch notes, and sometimes app settings.
Snapshot anything you change in `setup` and restore it in `teardown`.

# DG Roam Playwright Session

Use this skill to open a real Roam Research graph with one of the local Playwright test accounts.

Secrets must live only in the ignored `apps/roam/.env`. Do not print, inspect, or commit passwords, cookies, local storage, or Playwright profile contents.

## Quick Start

Open slot 1:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 1
```

Use slots 2 or 3 for isolated concurrent work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 2
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 3
```

The script writes screenshots and JSON proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

## Environment

The ignored `apps/roam/.env` should contain one set per slot:

```sh
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_EMAIL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PASSWORD_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_GRAPH_URL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_1=
```

Repeat for `_2` and `_3`.

Account emails and graph URLs are intentionally required from the ignored app `.env`. Do not add real test account identifiers, graph names, graph URLs, or passwords to committed files.

Profile directories default to ignored local paths under `local/roam-playwright/profiles/`.

## Safety Notes

- Only one Chromium process can own a persistent profile at a time.
- Use a different `--slot` for concurrent agents.
- Use `--headed --allow-login` if manual login recovery is needed.
- Do not run Supabase smoke tests as part of this skill; this skill is only for Roam login/session proof.

name: dg-obsidian-cdp-verify
description: Verify Obsidian plugin changes by driving the running app over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and asserting on real behaviour. Use when a change needs proving in the real app rather than by unit test — apps/obsidian has no test runner — or when a reviewer asks "does this actually work?".

# DG Obsidian CDP Verify

Use this skill to prove an `apps/obsidian` change works in a real Obsidian vault.

`apps/obsidian` has no test runner (roam, website, database and content-model do).
The way to prove a change works is to drive the real app: Obsidian is Electron, so
it speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol. About 150 lines covers `evaluate`, input
injection and condition polling — Playwright is not required.

## Prerequisites

1. **Relaunch Obsidian with the debug port.** Run the steps separately — the
   auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound command.
   ```bash
   osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to quit'
   ```
   ```bash
   open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222
   ```
   Ask the user before doing this: it closes their running app.
2. **Your build in the vault.** `apps/obsidian/.env` mirrors the dev build into
   the vault plugin dir. Confirm it is _your_ build — see the first gotcha.

## Quick Start

```sh
# 1. preflight: port up, right vault, YOUR bundle, plugin enabled
node skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/preflight.mjs "a string unique to your change"

# 2. run a verification
node skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs
```

Set `VAULT` to target a vault other than `testVault`.

Write the verification as scenarios and hand them to `runVerification`, which owns
everything order-dependent (plugin reload, stray-modal cleanup, sidebar collapse,
teardown, exit code):

```js
import { runVerification } from "./scripts/harness.mjs";

await runVerification({
  modalSelector: ".dg-node-search-modal",
  setup: async ({ client }) => ({
    /* snapshot anything you will mutate */
  }),
  teardown: async ({ client, state }) => {
    /* put it back */
  },
  scenarios: [
    {
      name: "01-does-the-thing",
      body: async ({ client, check, state }) => {
        await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById("…");`);
        await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".my-modal")`, {
          label: "modal",
        });
        check(
          "the thing happened",
          await client.evaluate(`…`),
          "detail on failure",
        );
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

`client` gives you `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `reloadPlugin` and
`pressEscape`. See `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` — the real
verification that shipped ENG-2114 (15 assertions, 3 scenarios). Copy it as the
starting point for a new one.

## Gotchas

Each of these cost real debugging time. The first three produced confident, wrong
diagnoses.

| Symptom                                               | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "My feature is missing from the build"                | **Every worktree's dev watcher mirrors into the same vault plugin dir.** Another branch's watcher silently overwrote your bundle. This is what `preflight.mjs` checks. Find competing watchers with `pgrep -fl "scripts/dev.ts"`; rebuild with `(cd apps/obsidian && pnpm build)`. |
| App appears to double-handle one keypress             | Your key helper spread `{ type, ...opts }`, so a caller's `type: "keyDown"` overrode the loop and sent two keydowns. `type` must come **after** the spread.                                                                                                                        |
| `editor.hasFocus()` is false but focus looks right    | CodeMirror ANDs with `document.hasFocus()`, so it reports false whenever Obsidian is not the frontmost macOS app — running a build in the terminal flips it. Assert `document.activeElement.closest(".cm-editor")` instead.                                                        |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks correct    | Obsidian saves on a debounce. Poll the file until it changes; never read straight after the action.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Assertions read a mix of two modals                   | A crashed earlier run left one mounted. `runVerification` clears strays first; a synthetic `body.click()` will not dismiss a modal, an Escape key event will.                                                                                                                      |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found"           | You detached every markdown leaf first. Use `getLeaf("tab")`, which reuses an empty active leaf.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Editing only files under `src/styles/` never rebuilds | The concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd`, outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Top-level `await` throws inside `evaluate`            | Bodies are wrapped in a plain function. Return a promise chain instead.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Wrong window driven                                   | Several page targets exist — one per open vault, plus popouts and settings. Select by `app.vault.getName()`, never by title.                                                                                                                                                       |

Two more, from experience rather than symptoms:

- **Reset state at the start of a scenario**, or assertions inherit leftover tabs
  and splits from the last run and a correct implementation reads as a failure.
- **The developer is using the app while you drive it.** A human opening a tab
  mid-run produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation.

## Safety Notes

- Ask before relaunching Obsidian: it closes the app the developer is using.
- Verification runs mutate the vault — scratch notes, sometimes app settings.
  Snapshot anything you change in `setup` and restore it in `teardown`.
- Point runs at a dev vault (`testVault`), never a real one.

Both agents reported, and I verified the load-bearing claims myself. Here's what's actually going on.

---

## 1. How tests get generated — the prompt isn't reachable from your machine

**The generator is not in `proof-kit`.** What's there is the *kit format* (the schema a generated test must satisfy), the *runner*, and 13 real generated kits as fixtures. The generator is a separate program, `qa.ts propose`, and the code points at it explicitly:

> `// Whether a case runs. qa.ts proposes cases from the PR's diff; a person approves or rejects each one…`
> — `proof-kit/prototypes/proof-runner/src/core/kit.ts:33`

It lives in `dg-demo-videos/proof/` at the absolute path `/mnt/data/projects/dg-demo-videos/` (a Linux path — and `sid` is hardcoded in the runner, so this is single-user tooling). I checked: that repo is **not on this machine, not under `DiscourseGraphs/`, not under `sid597/`, and not in GitHub search**. It's private to Sid's box. Nothing I can do from here gets you that prompt.

**Ask Sid for exactly three things:**
1. `proof/qa.ts` — the propose-cases-from-a-diff generator (the prompt itself)
2. `proof/README.md`, sections **"The page"** and **"The brain's loop"** — the runner's own bootstrap prompt defers step-authoring rules to these by name, so this is the authoring rubric
3. `proof/recipes/` — the reusable step vocabulary

**But the criteria are recoverable without the prompt,** because they're encoded as types and validators rather than prose. This is arguably the more useful half:

| Dimension | What the schema enforces |
|---|---|
| **What to cover** | Two sources: the Linear ticket's **Done When** bullets, plus **surface areas** — "an area next to the change that it could break, beyond the PR's own Done When", each tied to the diff's files |
| **Traceability** | Every case carries `proves` (which Done When) and `surface` (which risk area); results roll up per bullet, and a bullet holds only when every case under it passed |
| **Review gate** | `proposed` → `approved` / `rejected`, with **a reason required on rejection**. The model proposes; a person decides. Rejected cases stay in the kit with their reason "so the record shows what was left out and why" |
| **Assertion strength** | Three explicit tiers: `expect.js` (machine) > `expect.text` (human judges by eye) > nothing, where the last is flagged in the UI as *"Nothing is checked at the end: it passes if every step runs."* |
| **Integrity** | An unknown attribute is a parse error, "so a typo can't leave a case without its check"; a tester-assisted pass is counted separately from a clean pass; **kit bugs are separated from product bugs**; skips require a written reason; an agent may not issue verdicts and agent-authored JS needs human Allow; never run against production |

The one prompt that *is* in the repo (`src/roam/links.ts:43-49`) is for an agent **driving** an existing kit, not authoring cases.

---

## 2. What was adopted to Obsidian

Two distinct layers got built, and it's worth separating them:

**Layer A — your `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` skill.** This grew out of the ENG-2114 work and is now considerably more than what we built in August: `claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup`, vault leasing with an atomic lock, the marker preflight run *twice* (before and after plugin reload), a bundle sha1 compared before/after that invalidates the whole run if another watcher overwrites `main.js` mid-flight, baseline workspace restore between scenarios, and a scenario matrix that feeds `pr-evidence` → `create-pr`. The Obsidian-specific problems it solves: getting Electron onto a debug port, picking the right vault window among many CDP targets, mirroring the build into `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/`, plugin id ≠ folder name on reload, and keeping the renderer unthrottled when Obsidian isn't frontmost.

**Layer B — Sid's Obsidian runner, which sits on top of yours.** I confirmed this directly:

```
obsidian/cli.ts:3   // Launch, vault lease and build delivery are dg-obsidian-cdp-verify's; this adds…
obsidian/cli.ts:33  const HARNESS = process.env.DG_CDP_VERIFY_DIR ?? ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts
```

So the adoption already happened, and the division is clean: **your skill owns the Obsidian plumbing; proof-kit owns the cases, the traceability and the PR output.** There are already three Obsidian kit fixtures (`eng-2143`, `eng-2176`, `eng-2228`).

### What I'd do next — and the urgent item isn't a feature

**Neither half is in version control.** That's the real finding:

- Your skill: `~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` is **not a git repo and not tracked anywhere**. PR #1327 — the one we opened in August — was **closed unmerged on 2026-10-16**, and that commit is a materially older architecture anyway (a `preflight.mjs`, no leasing). Meanwhile the live copy has ~51 recorded runs across 6 branches, most recent today. It is in daily service with **no backup**.
- Sid's Obsidian runner: the entire `obsidian/` directory is **untracked**, on a branch `obsidian-runner` that has never merged and has no remote.

So: **get both under version control before adding anything.** For yours, that's reviving #1327 against the current architecture. The question that killed it the first time — "should a skill in `skills/` ship executable scripts?" — now has a much better answer than it did in August: 51 runs of daily use, and a second tool depending on it by path.

After that, the ordering I'd suggest:
1. **Get `qa.ts` from Sid** and point it at an Obsidian PR — that's the missing generation step, and it's the whole reason your scenarios are currently hand-written and thrown away.
2. **Converge the two contracts.** Your harness takes `{name, run, expect}` as `.mjs`; proof-kit takes declarative JSON steps. Today's scenarios are scratchpad-only and discarded after the run, so nothing accumulates. Kits are durable and traceable to Done When. Adopting the kit format is what turns one-off verification into a regression suite.
3. **Fix the two admitted gaps**: Obsidian runs only support `in-session` fixtures ("other phases need the proof database, which Obsidian runs don't start yet"), and `_verify/<branch>/` notes are never cleaned up, so they accumulate in every vault.

---

## 3. How to QA the testing feature itself

The key point: **a verification harness fails by passing.** A broken test that goes red announces itself; a test that can't go red is invisible and actively harmful, because it buys false confidence on a PR. So QA should target false passes, not crashes.

**The primary technique is mutation testing.** Deliberately break the product code and confirm each scenario goes red. Right now your harness has an excellent story for *"am I testing the right bundle?"* — marker preflight twice, bundle hash invalidation, competing-watcher scan — and **no story at all** for *"can this assertion ever fail?"* Concretely: take the ENG-2114 example, invert the link-format logic in `apps/obsidian`, rebuild, rerun, and confirm the wikilink/markdown scenarios fail. Any scenario that still passes is decorative. This is cheap to run as a one-off and would be the single highest-value QA pass.

Specific weak spots worth probing, drawn from the run data:

| Risk | Why it matters | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| **Flaky first run** | The 51 recorded runs show a pattern of first-run-fails-then-passes-seconds-later, which the skill's own gotchas acknowledge | Run the same unchanged scenario 10× and measure the failure rate. A harness with a real flake rate trains people to rerun until green — which destroys the signal |
| **Compound `expect`** | The ENG-2114 scenarios pack ~14 assertions into 3 matrix rows via `&&` chains | One false conjunct fails the whole row with no indication which. Split, or report per-conjunct |
| **Selector drift** | Admitted in the gotchas: "Selectors from an old ENG example don't match. The UI drifts." | Scenarios that silently stop matching anything should fail loudly, not quietly pass |
| **No-check cases** | proof-kit explicitly flags cases where "it passes if every step runs" | Audit for assertions that only prove the steps executed |

**Use proof-kit's own metrics as your QA scorecard** — it already distinguishes a clean pass from a tester-assisted pass, and kit bugs from product bugs. Those two ratios *are* the health metric for the harness: if "passed by the tester" or "the kit needs N fixes" climbs, the harness is degrading regardless of how green the matrix looks.

One structural note for QA: your harness only has proof-kit's **tier-1** assertions (`expect` returns a boolean). It has no "human judges this by eye" tier. That's fine for text and cursor positions, but it means anything visual — the thing screenshots are being captured for — is currently *unasserted*; a human looks at the PNG in the PR, which is judgement with no record of the verdict. Adopting the `judge` tier would close that.

---

The counts — 51 runs, 13 kits, 17 Vitest files — come from their reports; the Vitest one I confirmed, and CI does run those via `ci:validate` in [ci.yaml:35](.github/workflows/ci.yaml:35).
